shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade front-month corn futures traded at a three-year high on Tuesday on a poor U.S. crop and spillover strength from soaring wheat futures.

children: Chicago Board of Trade front-month corn futures traded at a three-year high on Tuesday on a poor U.S. crop and spillover strength from soaring wheat futures.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture kept its good-to-excellent rating for the nation's corn crop unchanged at 57% in a weekly report on Monday. That was down from 69% a year ago.
Crops were drying down before harvesting in the Midwest, with hot and dry weather expected over the next week.
The consultancy StoneX raised its estimate for Brazil's 2026/27 first corn crop to 29.3 million tons, from 28.7 million tons in its previous forecast.
settled 8.25 cents higher to $5.46 per bushel.
